summary: Safe to run as a scored combo: every new cell is gated in prepare(), the expert-weight copy fits easily, and M1 can be read directly from the profile and its PATH CHOSEN line. Three things must change before the build: (1) decide align2 BEFORE the rega checks, or keep rega on align_par; (2) put back the standalone port's align-equivalence step; (3) make the copy check robust to decode's state, which holds a torch.cuda.Stream. The B128 conjecture rests on a false premise, and M2's join-slack conjecture cannot be read from a ~1.5 us residual.
justification: M1 mechanism: plausible but the expected size is overstated. At T=256 decode's incumbent is a stronger Marlin than the one moe beat. moe's _fwd_block_size_m gives bsm 32 at T=256 (64 -> two-smaller), but decode is capped at 16 (marlin-block-m-cap-16), and decode's Marlin pair is 409.2 / 442.7 us (sliding/full, job 933d) against moe's 457 (selector) / 483 us (judged). The 'expected' line takes moe's absolute margin (457 - 402 = 55 us) instead of comparing against decode's own incumbent. If rega costs about what it did in moe (~402 us, with moe's busier routing), sliding verify_32 gains only ~7 us (1.7%, below the 1.02 gate) and full ~40 us. A realistic outcome is therefore B256 = REGA on one or neither layer's routing, or a win smaller than 40-55 us; the selector protects the downside either way. The expert-block floor is ~170 us (32 experts x ~816 MiB NVFP4 at 4.8 TB/s), so there is room in principle. WEAKEST LINK: the Conjecture's first premise is false. It says decode's B128 incumbent 'is a different Marlin (block_m capped at 16, so at T=128 it launches more blocks than moe's)'. But moe's T=128 also runs bsm 16 (SGLang picks 48, two-smaller gives 16), so the B128 Marlin config is identical in both problems. The remaining arguments are flatter, fewer local routes (plausible, but it shrinks both arms) and 'input arrives after a side-stream join' (irrelevant: the selector times the expert block in isolation). With moe measuring rega at 0.80-0.81x Marlin at B128, the prediction 'B128 = REGA' is weakly supported. The run CAN refute it cleanly (the [rega] B128 line with both numbers and local-route counts), which is fine, but the author should expect MARLIN. M2: align2 saves ~1.8 us on a side branch (~26 us) that races the pooler nvjet (~35 us at T=256) plus the pre-expert norm. It is most likely hidden, and even if it is on the critical path the verify_32 row moves ~1.5 us on 607-869 us, far inside the +/-1.5% CI (9-13 us). The proposed read-out (row delta minus the selector's expert-block delta, residual ~1.5 us) therefore cannot be resolved by this run. Either drop M2 or make it testable inside prepare(): time the whole T=256 FFN front as one graph (pooler + norm on main || router + routing + align on side -> join) with align_par vs align2, and print both. That measures the join slack directly. Time and memory: fine. Master's whole check took 216 s wall (prepare 4.5 s). Adding the C1 modules, the rega load_inline (~45-60 s) and ~85 s of prepare phases still lands well under 300 s for prepare and 15 min for the run, and the per-phase deadlines will not bite. The extra NVFP4 bank is w13 512 MiB + w2 256 MiB + scales ~48 MiB = ~0.8 GiB per state. The judge prepares once and clones the state (the 933d log shows a single prepare with cumulative 4.5 s), so the second copy is +0.8 GiB, plus ~0.8 GiB of transient clones in prepare(). That is about 2.4 GiB peak extra on an H200 (141 GB), alongside the existing 512 MB cos_sin table per state: no memory concern. WG_CAP_ROWS 8192 and WG_MAX_BLOCKS 384 cover decode's T=512 bsm-16 align (cap 4576 rows, 286 blocks). Shapes match moe: hidden 4096 into the experts, size_n 4096, 32 local experts. Copy-safety: moe s5's per-call tensor-map encode into a stack-local grid constant, with per-state wg_xs / wg_hs / wg_err and no stored map, is the right design for the judge's clone-and-rotate. Under capture the encode bakes the capturing state's pointers into that graph, which is what the judge does.
confounders: stack-align-par-sidestream-sliding1 (landed): decode's T>32 align is _align_parallel on the SIDE stream, consumed after main_stream.wait_stream. moe's rega path never consumed that align: _moe_wgmma calls SGLang moe_align_block_size(local_ids, 16, 32) inline on the main stream. Its outputs are the same capacity (n + 32*15) with sentinel n and block_experts -1 past used, so they should match what rega reads (it is bounded by n_padded and skips -1 blocks). The combo nevertheless dropped the standalone port's step (3), the bit-for-bit check that rega fed align_par equals rega fed moe_align_block_size(local_ids, 16, 32). Restore it; it is cheap.

M2 align2 vs M1 rega (the moe designer's note, confirmed in moe master): in moe, align2 runs only inside _moe_marlin, never on the wgmma path, so align2 -> rega has never run anywhere. In this combo, kernel_fn's dispatch would feed align2's output to rega at v256 whenever both flags are set. M1's phase (deadline 200 s) runs its canary, three-state copy check and selector BEFORE M2's phase (250 s) sets the align2 flag, so the composed align2 -> rega path is never validated or timed. Fix: run M2's phase first, so M1's checks and selector go through the final dispatch. Or pin _experts_rega's dispatch to _align_parallel whatever the align2 flag says, as moe effectively did. The bit-identity proof covers the composition only if it compares all four buffers in full (sentinel tail and block_experts past used included), as moe's _align2_first_mismatch does; require that.

marlin-block-m-cap-16 (landed): sets decode's B256 incumbent at bsm 16, where moe's is bsm 32. It is the reason moe's 0.88x will not transfer directly at T=256 (decode's Marlin is ~10-15% faster than moe's). At B128 the incumbent configs are IDENTICAL (both bsm 16), contrary to the Conjecture. The WG_BSM == _block_size_m(T) assert is correct and needed.

C1's S3 (pre-attention fused kernels, per-class gated): if any S3 class reaches T=128/256, the verify_16/32 rows carry S3 as well as M1. It does not confound M1 attribution, because the profile separates wg_gather / wg_kernel from Marlin and the pre-attention kernels. Read M1 from the kernel rows, not the shape row.

small-t dense chain / dl3 pieces / w2 atomic T=1 / post-expert-norm-triton-small-t: T<=32 only. They do not interact with M1/M2 except through the L2/TLB-footprint hypothesis in the Conjecture, which the cold-L2 judge makes unlikely.

full-decode sk ticket kernels and fa3-hdim128-head-pairing-batched: these touch the attention side of full verify_16/32 rows before the MoE. No interaction with the rega launch sequence (rega starts after the router/align join).
interference: No companion warranted. M1 is directly attributable: its PATH CHOSEN line gives decode's own rega-vs-Marlin medians per class, and the judged profile shows wg_kernel / wg_gather time replacing Marlin + act_and_mul on the verify_16/32 rows. A null, gain or loss on those rows is therefore readable at kernel level whatever S1-S3 do. C1's sources live on T<=32 rows (and are measured by C1 itself). M2 is not attributable by any one extra run: its effect (~1.5 us at most) is below the per-shape CI. A companion would spend a scored run to measure noise, so the fix is the in-prepare FFN-front join timing described in the justification, or dropping M2. The standalone moe-rega-bucket-gate-port-t128-t512 (queued, p1) is a strict subset of this combo's M1. Once this runs, mark it superseded rather than spend another run on identical M1 code.
rules_flags: No per-call mutable state found: the gates read cfg/shape and this state's prepare() flags only. The per-call tensor-map encode into a stack-local grid constant is a kernel argument, not process-global state, and there is no BLAS-backend or cuBLASLt preference toggle. It complies with the standing policy as written; keep it that way. The rega module must not stash a 'last encoded map' or pointer in a module static (moe s4's failure).
Expert-weight clones are prepare()-only and freed; the retile is a lossless repack of NVFP4 codes and E4M3 scales (dequant in registers only). Allowed.
_experts_rega allocates cache3 [T*8, 4096] per call: shape-sized, allowed. align2's count table is also shape-sized per call (moe's design). Allowed.

None of the 13 pre-timing tests has 128 <= T <= 512 (T values: 1, 1, 8, 9, 24, 40, 33, 16, 8, 32, 1, 32, 16), so the rega path is first exercised by the judge on the timed verify_16/32 calls, which are reference-checked. On a SCORED submit a rega correctness miss burns the submit, so the prepare-time fp32-dequant check and the two-state alternating replay are the only guard. Make sure they run on judge-like 'dist soft' routings at T=128 and 256 with local_start in {0, 96, 224}, and through the side-stream dispatch exactly as kernel_fn issues it.
The hypothesis text says 'First measurement is an okc check', but today's checks are spent and this is a scored submit. The builder should not wait for a check.
open_questions: The three-state copy check cannot be 'copied verbatim'. moe's version captures moe's kernel_fn on (A, copy.deepcopy(state) with the ext memoised, judge-model clone C). Decode's state holds a torch.cuda.Stream ('side_stream'), the dense-chain / sk / dl3 load_inline module handles and nn.Module boundaries. A raw copy.deepcopy may raise, which silently turns M1 off as a 'fallback'. Should the check run decode's T=128/256 expert path (side-stream dispatch + _experts_rega) on states built by the judge-model tensor-cloning walk only, with the stream and ext handles shared via memo? Whatever is chosen, the fallback line must print the exception text.
Does the M1 selector time rega with the align that kernel_fn will actually use (align2 at v256 if M2 is enabled)? Running M2 before M1 answers this.

Is there one shared clock for all the prepare() deadlines? C1 120/150/180 s, M1 200 s, M2 250 s are all measured from t_prepare0, but master's prepare finishes in ~5 s, so these deadlines only matter if a phase hangs. Is any phase's own internal timeout (e.g. an mbarrier-hang canary) bounded?

Expected B256 win: compare against decode's own Marlin (409 / 443 us), not moe's 457. If the selector prints REGA only for the full-layer routing's local-route count, is the flag per class (shared by both layers) or per (class, layer)? The spec is per class, so one routing mix decides for both layers. Print the local-route counts that drove it.

If M2 is kept: will its selector enable align2 even when the side branch is fully hidden behind the pooler, adding a cell that changes nothing measurable? Prefer gating it on the FFN-front join timing.
